correctness.rationale: The Fourier-product nonvanishing lemma follows by absolute summability of each factor difference from one. Divisibility by X^(2^(j-1))+1 is equivalent to coefficient equality on antipodal dyadic residue pairs. Independent Haar 2-adic digits give exact binomial class splits; odd prefix classes preclude every later hit. Finite live even partitions yield an absorbing rational recursion with self-loops 2^(b-K)<1; the positive minimum immediate-hit probability ensures geometric tail control, giving natural centered-cube density. For K=8 all four reachable live states and the generating function were rederived separately, exact fractions checked, and direct residue enumeration performed. The standalone Python checker is part of this package; its finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Lam--Leung implies the zero criterion for a single 2-power mask, and affine-IFS product theory implies that integer-transform zeros are the union of such mask zeros, but neither gives their density without evaluating overlapping first-hit events. The existing general-base maximum-magnitude theorem is not a zero-density theorem. The prime-base theorem with p=2 specializes to K=2, while its odd-prime bases are not base 2; the three-atom positive finite-cycle record and four-point cyclic indicator record do not imply the K=8 dyadic IFS result.

value.rationale: Integer Fourier-null density is a natural asymptotic invariant: it is the proportion of torus Fourier characters annihilated by convolution with a canonical singular affine self-similar measure. The all-even-K finite-state rationality mechanism is structurally motivated and explains nontrivial scale-overlap phenomena, whereas the K=8 generating function determines every first-zero frequency census and the precise seven-dimensional null-space proportion. Neither a single mask zero condition nor isolated finite enumeration provides the complete distribution; exact fractions were not chosen as arbitrary numerical slices.
